what_matters.head: Chip stocks fell for a ninth straight session on Friday. The iShares chip fund lost 4.1% on the day and 16.3% across the nine sessions, and software stocks fell with them.
what_matters.detail: Bank of America's chip analysts said rising interest rates, geopolitics, pushback against data centres and strain at some lower-rated GPU-rental companies (such as CoreWeave) had revived comparisons with the dot-com era. In a Yahoo Finance basket of 45 software stocks, 43 fell, losing more than $260 billion of market value, about $83 billion of it Microsoft's. The VIX rose more than four points, its biggest one-day rise in points since 5 June. Yahoo Finance said the chip fund's only earlier nine-session losing run ended in May 2006; the nine-session count is from our own reports.

what_matters.head: Brent crude touched $110 on Friday for the first time since May and settled 3.7% higher at $109.86. US crude rose 3.5% to $101.41, up 10.4% over the week.
what_matters.detail: Reuters tied the rise to Iran stepping up attacks on shipping around the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran said answered the US blockade of its ports; the data firm Kpler said the attacks had cut Gulf crude flows sharply. Ukraine also struck Russia's Ryazan refinery on Thursday. The card's 5-day figure for oil (+3.5%) is wrong; see Data notes.

what_matters.head: Meta reports after the New York close on Wednesday, the first of Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon to report since the sell-off. Alphabet and Microsoft follow on 28 Oct and Amazon on 29 Oct.
what_matters.detail: Analysts expect revenue of about $63.4B (range $61.7–65.3B, 48 analysts) and earnings per share of about $5.70, against the company's forecast of $61–64B. Meta's 2026 spending plan for data centres and equipment is $130–145B. The quarter also carries a legal charge of about $10B that Meta said was not in its expense forecast.

latest.tape_note: US stocks fell on Friday: the Nasdaq lost 2.1%, the S&P 500 1.1% and the Dow about 0.3%. Over the week the Nasdaq fell 4.5%, its worst week since June, the S&P 500 2.0%, while the Dow rose 0.7%. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'I don't prejudge meetings', and futures traders put the chance of an October rate rise at 17%, down from 28% on Thursday (CME FedWatch, via Investopedia). The 10-year Treasury yield ended at 5.10%. Gold rose 0.3% and the US dollar fell 0.2% against the Singapore dollar.

recent.headline: Chip stocks fell for a ninth straight session on Friday. The iShares chip fund lost 4.1% on the day and 16.3% across the nine sessions, and software stocks fell with them.
Aixtron fell 12.7% in Frankfurt on Thursday, 3.3 times its usual day. Half an hour after the close it said its third-quarter orders and profit were well above expectations.

Chip and AI stocks fell hard on Wednesday. US consumer prices rose more than expected in September, which raised bets on another Fed rate rise, and worries about how AI data centres are paid for spread.
MAS left its Singapore-dollar policy unchanged this morning. All 10 analysts in a Reuters poll last week had expected it to tighten again, after a very slight tightening in July.

SK Hynix fell about 9% and Samsung about 8% by 13:05 Seoul time, after China's CXMT said it plans to launch a denser kind of server memory by the end of 2026. The Kospi was down 7.2% around midday, its lowest level since July.
